\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[a4paper,margin=25mm]{geometry}
\usepackage{booktabs,tabularx,amsmath,longtable,url,float}
\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
\title{Supplementary Material S1\\Restricted human review of Stage 1 mappings}
\author{}
\date{17 October 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\section{Scope and provenance}
This is a post-hoc descriptive supplement to the mapping evaluation, not a complete
gold reference or a replacement for the main 60-source experiment. Eight sources
were selected with fixed shuffle seed 20261017 from the remaining 58 after excluding
previously exposed OR001 and OR002. Selection preceded scoring. The sources are
OR012, OR047, OR059, OR032, OR016, OR030, OR018 and OR011. The union of four saved
methods' predictions contains 75 source--pair candidates. Two reviewers supplied
13 distinct additional pairs, giving an observed union of 88 items. The taxonomy
contains 183 legal component--intent pairs per source; the 88-item union does not
exhaust that frame.

The DeepSeek predictions match historical v3 Stage 1 mappings reused upstream by
v4. The missing duplicated mapping field in v4 does not make this upstream input
untraceable, and this provenance does not establish equivalence of complete v3
and v4 experiments. Qwen denotes the saved mapping baseline, not downstream
generation or the automated quality evaluator. BM25 and embedding predictions
are also frozen. No new model calls or experimental reruns were made.

\section{Human process and limits of the records}
The two reviewers are postgraduate students with backgrounds in marine and
systems engineering and fellow students of an author. The authors confirmed
separate human review followed by discussion, and confirmed that both reviewers
checked the complete taxonomy for all eight sources and checked for omissions.
This retrospective confirmation is recorded separately from the four unchanged
submitted workbooks. It is not a timestamped measurement of review duration,
exposure order or independent reliability. Reviewer C reassessed judgements after
feedback; the submitted pre-discussion file is therefore not a pristine blind
initial judgement record.

Some original worksheet notes conflict with the subsequently confirmed human
process (including a non-human-record note and a DeepSeek attribution). They are
preserved in the reproducibility archive, together with the separate author
confirmation; they have not been silently rewritten. Blank timing and first-pass
fields remain blank. No review-time, strong blinding or external expert claim is
made. C and D identify the actual reviewers; the corresponding template slots
are A and B respectively.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{Candidate labels in the submitted records (75 items each).}
\begin{tabular}{llrrr}\toprule
Reviewer & Record & Relevant & Not relevant & Uncertain\\\midrule
C & Before discussion &25&31&19\\
C & After discussion &25&31&19\\
D & Before discussion &34&26&15\\
D & After discussion &26&31&18\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Exact label agreement is 59/75 (78.7\%) before discussion and 74/75 (98.7\%)
after discussion. The latter includes 18 jointly uncertain candidates and is
neither model accuracy nor independent inter-rater reliability. The remaining
candidate disagreement is OR032, \path{flow_meter:alarm_setpoint} (C uncertain;
D relevant). The submitted D files contain 15 changed candidate labels: two
not-relevant to uncertain, six relevant to uncertain, five uncertain to
not-relevant and two relevant to not-relevant. Narrative worksheet notes are
not substituted for these cell-level counts.

The missing-pair lists contain four entries from C and 12 from D, with three
shared entries and 13 distinct entries overall. Only one additional pair is
jointly definite relevant: OR032, \path{control_system:manual_override}.
The other two shared entries are C-uncertain/D-relevant. An unlisted item is
unknown, not a negative label. Omission checking does not turn these lists into
an exhaustive binary reference.

\section{Common definite-label mask}
Let $M$ contain items on which both post-discussion records give the same definite
label. It contains 56 candidate items and the one jointly relevant missing pair:
57/88 observed items (64.8\%), with 26 positive and 31 negative labels. All eight
sources are retained. For every method $j$, use the same $M$ and positive set $G$:
\[
 TP_j=|P_j\cap G|,\quad FP_j=|(P_j\cap M)\setminus G|,\quad
 FN_j=|G\setminus P_j|.
\]
Micro precision, recall and $F_1$ are computed from these pooled counts. Predictions
outside $M$ are unscored, not successes or errors. This mask was defined post hoc;
agreement and certainty may select easier items. Its conditional recall is not
recall against the full taxonomy or the 60-source set. The eight sources, not the
individual candidate items, are the sampling units; no power or significance
claim is made.

\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\caption{Restricted counts and micro metrics on the same 57-item mask.}
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}\toprule
Method & TP & FP & FN & Precision & Recall & $F_1$\\\midrule
DeepSeek &21&1&5&0.9545&0.8077&0.8750\\
Qwen &18&3&8&0.8571&0.6923&0.7660\\
BM25 &6&20&20&0.2308&0.2308&0.2308\\
Embedding &12&11&14&0.5217&0.4615&0.4898\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}\end{table}

\begin{table}[h]\centering
\caption{Prediction coverage; excluded predictions are unscored.}
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}\toprule
Method & Total & Included in $M$ & Excluded from $M$\\\midrule
DeepSeek &33&22&11\\Qwen &26&21&5\\BM25 &32&26&6\\Embedding &32&23&9\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}\end{table}

\begin{table}[h]\centering
\caption{Source-level candidate and common-mask coverage. The mask also includes one missing pair for OR032.}
\begin{tabular}{lrrrr}\toprule
Source & Candidates & Mask items & Positive & Negative\\\midrule
OR012&11&9&5&4\\OR047&9&6&2&4\\OR059&8&6&3&3\\OR032&12&11&7&4\\
OR016&9&6&1&5\\OR030&8&5&1&4\\OR018&11&10&6&4\\OR011&7&4&1&3\\\midrule
Total&75&57&26&31\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}\end{table}
\section{Reviewer-specific and uncertainty sensitivity analyses}
Reviewer-specific definite subsets are secondary checks with different masks;
they must not replace the shared-mask comparison. C has 58 definite observed
items (27 positive, 31 negative), while D has 61 (30 positive, 31 negative).
\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\caption{Micro metrics using each reviewer's own definite subset.}
\begin{tabular}{llrrr}\toprule
Reviewer & Method & Precision & Recall & $F_1$\\\midrule
C&DeepSeek&0.9545&0.7778&0.8571\\C&Qwen&0.8571&0.6667&0.7500\\
C&BM25&0.2308&0.2222&0.2264\\C&Embedding&0.5217&0.4444&0.4800\\\midrule
D&DeepSeek&0.9545&0.7000&0.8077\\D&Qwen&0.8571&0.6000&0.7059\\
D&BM25&0.2308&0.2000&0.2143\\D&Embedding&0.5417&0.4333&0.4815\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}\end{table}

For sensitivity within the 88-item observed union only, keep each reviewer's
definite labels fixed and let every uncertain or unlisted item vary. C has 30
unknown items and D has 27. For method $j$, a pessimistic completion makes unknown
unpredicted items positive and unknown predicted items negative; the optimistic
completion reverses those assignments. These give the extrema below. Completions
are method-specific, not a single shared gold set. These ranges are not confidence
intervals, do not quantify sampling uncertainty and do not measure full-taxonomy
recall. They must not be presented as v4 output-quality estimates.

\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\caption{Uncertainty extrema within the observed 88-item union only.}
\begin{tabular}{llrrr}\toprule
Reviewer & Method & Precision range & Recall range & $F_1$ range\\\midrule
C&DeepSeek&0.6364--0.9697&0.4565--0.8421&0.5316--0.9014\\
C&Qwen&0.6923--0.8846&0.3462--0.7188&0.4615--0.7931\\
C&BM25&0.1875--0.3750&0.1176--0.3636&0.1446--0.3692\\
C&Embedding&0.3750--0.6563&0.2500--0.5833&0.3000--0.6176\\\midrule
D&DeepSeek&0.6364--0.9697&0.4565--0.7805&0.5316--0.8649\\
D&Qwen&0.6923--0.8846&0.3462--0.6571&0.4615--0.7541\\
D&BM25&0.1875--0.3750&0.1176--0.3333&0.1446--0.3529\\
D&Embedding&0.4063--0.6563&0.2653--0.5526&0.3210--0.6000\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}\end{table}

\section{Reproducibility and interpretation}
The accompanying reproducibility archive retains the four original workbooks,
their SHA-256 manifest, the frozen sample and predictions, normalized annotations,
mask membership, exact results, process addendum and deterministic analysis and
verification scripts. The frozen prediction SHA-256 is
\begin{quote}\small\path{b21c48345159bc050ea8110fe801ac3d84f7b5da9cfa22d2bf6b8b4eec2cb458}\end{quote}
The frozen sample manifest SHA-256 is
\begin{quote}\small\path{026b8e9cabcf0d856cf160baa1490a2e1f5ff8f3c605a40d8234bb3c916a4d2d}\end{quote}
These restricted descriptive analyses do not convert the incomplete reference
into a completed formal gold set. Peer recruitment, feedback exposure, candidate
priming, residual uncertainty, small source count and post-hoc restriction limit
generalization. Human assessments of taxonomy agreement, downstream correctness
and few-shot example quality (S1/S3/S4 instruments in the main study) remain
conditional follow-up work; this supplement does not claim those studies were
completed. ``Supplementary Material S1'' names this document and is distinct from
the main study's S1 annotation instrument.
\end{document}
